blocks.orig: The Udzungwa Mountains National Park is a beautiful area in the southern part of Tanzania. It has various habitats such as tropical rainforest, mountain and miombo forest, grassland and steppe. There are more than 400 species of birds, thousands species of plants and six species of monkeys – including the rare Iringa red colobus and the Sanje crested mangabey. These two types can only be found in this region. The Udzungwa national park has the second-largest biodiversity of any national park in Africa. A very interesting national park to visit during a Tanzania Safari!
blocks.html: In the south of Tanzania lies the Udzungwa Mountains National Park, a scenic area with a range of habitats: tropical rainforest, mountain and miombo forest, grassland and steppe. The park holds more than 400 bird species, thousands of plant species and six kinds of monkey, among them the rare Iringa red colobus and the Sanje crested mangabey, two primates that occur nowhere else but this region. Of all the national parks in Africa, Udzungwa ranks second for biodiversity. It makes a fascinating stop on a Tanzania Safari!

blocks.orig: Udzungwa Mountains has a good variety of wildlife. They are home to many animals, including Abbott’s duiker, Kipunji and unusual animals such as the grey-faced sengi. Elephants are living in the forests along the southern escarpment. Also, six registered primate species call Udzungwa national park their home. The Iringa red colobus and the Sanje crested mangabey live only in this area and nowhere else in the world! The latter, remarkably, remained undiscovered by biologists before 1979.
blocks.html: Wildlife in the Udzungwa Mountains is pleasingly varied. Many animals live here, including Abbott's duiker, the Kipunji and oddities such as the grey-faced sengi. Elephants roam the forests along the southern escarpment, and six recorded primate species make Udzungwa national park their home. The Iringa red colobus and the Sanje crested mangabey are found in this area and nowhere else on earth! Remarkably, biologists had no knowledge of the mangabey until 1979.

blocks.orig: The Kihansi spray toad lives around a waterfall on the Kihansi River. It was briefly extinct in the wild in 2009 when an upstream dam altered its habitat. Scientists successfully managed to reintroduce them back after a successful captive breeding program.
blocks.html: Near a waterfall on the Kihansi River lives the Kihansi spray toad. In 2009 the species was briefly extinct in the wild, after a dam upstream changed its habitat. Following a successful captive breeding programme, scientists were able to reintroduce the toads to the area.

blocks.orig: As a bird lover, you will be drawn to Udzungwa Mountains National Park for its abundance of birds, which includes more than 400 species. Bird-watchers regard the area among the top three African mainland bird conservation areas.
blocks.html: If you love birds, the sheer number of them in Udzungwa Mountains National Park will draw you in: more than 400 species live here. Bird-watchers rank the area among the three most important bird conservation areas on the African mainland.

blocks.orig: Some of the bird species in Udzungwa include the African marabou, Crowned eagle, Ruppells vulture and the African hobby. Scientists discovered the Francolin and Rufous-winged Sunbird only in the last few years. It also holds species such as Dappled mountain-robin, Sharpe’s akalat, Olive-flanked robin-chat and White-chested alethe. The Udzungwa forest partridge was only discovered in 1991 and is a species, with its closest relatives appearing to be the hill partridges of Asia.
blocks.html: Among the birds you may encounter in Udzungwa are the African marabou, the Crowned eagle, Ruppells vulture and the African hobby. The Francolin and the Rufous-winged Sunbird were only described by scientists in recent years. The park also shelters species such as the Dappled mountain-robin, Sharpe's akalat, the Olive-flanked robin-chat and the White-chested alethe. The Udzungwa forest partridge was first found as recently as 1991, and its nearest relatives appear to be the hill partridges of Asia.

blocks.orig: Most of the rainfall occurs in the November and March-to-May wet season, although mist and light rain occur at higher elevations during the dry season months. Temperatures are cooler at higher elevations. A visit to the park is not recommended in the rainy season. Best time is June to October.
blocks.html: The bulk of the rain falls in November and during the March-to-May wet season, though mist and light showers do occur at higher altitudes in the dry months. Higher up, the temperatures are cooler. We would not recommend visiting in the rainy season; June to October is the best period.

blocks.orig: My name is Harrison, and I am a guide at Udzungwa National Park for 9 years. Most of our guests come here to see the many species of bird – and of course the rare Iringa red colobus!
blocks.html: I'm Harrison, and I've been guiding in Udzungwa National Park for 9 years. The majority of our guests come for the many bird species, and naturally for the rare Iringa red colobus!

blocks.orig: Besides bird watching, Udzungwa is a magnet for hikers. Udzungwa National Park has no paved roads and is only accessible on foot. An excellent network of forest trails includes the popular half-day hike to the Sanje Waterfall, which tumbles 170 meters through a misty spray into the wooded valley below. It is one of the larger waterfalls in Tanzania and lays hidden from the rest of the world in dense rain forest.
blocks.html: Udzungwa draws hikers as well as bird watchers. There are no paved roads in Udzungwa National Park, so you explore it on foot. A fine network of forest trails includes the well-loved half-day walk to the Sanje Waterfall, which drops 170 metres in a cloud of mist into the wooded valley beneath. It ranks among Tanzania's larger waterfalls and stays hidden from the outside world in thick rain forest.

blocks.orig: The Udzungwa National Park is best known for its many species of birds and plants and the rare Iringa red colobus and the Sanje crested mangabey. Enjoy a hike through the rain forest to the 170 m tall Sanje Waterfall.
blocks.html: Udzungwa National Park is known above all for its wealth of bird and plant species and for the rare Iringa red colobus and Sanje crested mangabey. Take a walk through the rain forest to the Sanje Waterfall, 170 m high.

blocks.orig: Udzungwa National Park borders Mikumi National Park and Ruaha National Park can be reached by car. The three locations make a varied and pleasant safari circuit. If you wish, you can also add Selous Game Reserve to the route.
blocks.html: Udzungwa National Park shares a border with Mikumi National Park, and Ruaha National Park is within driving distance. Together these three spots form a varied and enjoyable safari circuit, and if you like you can add Selous Game Reserve to the route as well.
